title: Religious Language Synoptic
welcome_lead: Pull together verification, falsification, analogy, symbol, and language games for the religious language paper.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on religious language: cognitive and non-cognitive approaches.

concepts.def: The view that religious statements are truth-apt: capable of being true or false.
The view that religious statements are not truth-apt but express attitudes, intentions, or play other roles.
Ayer's positivist test: meaningful statements are analytic or empirically verifiable (1936).
Flew's view: assertions must concede what would count against them (1950-51).
Aquinas' theory: religious language uses terms in related, proportionate senses (Summa Theologica I, q. 13).
Tillich's view: symbols participate in the reality they signify (Dynamics of Faith, 1957).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Aquinas' analogy and Swinburne's univocal-with-stretch approach defend the cognitive status of religious language. 'God is good' makes a genuine, if analogical, claim about the divine nature.

Cognitivism is essential to the realist self-understanding of most historic Christianity.

R.M. Hare's bliks, Wittgenstein's language games, and D.Z. Phillips' Wittgensteinian fideism construe religious language non-cognitively. To say 'God exists' is to commit oneself to a way of life rather than describe a metaphysical fact.

Tillich's symbolism and Randall's view of religion as a quasi-poetic enterprise sit on this side too.

Cognitivism preserves the rationality of theistic disputes but exposes religious claims to scientific testing. Non-cognitivism shields religion from positivist attack but, critics argue, at the cost of its objectivity.

Hybrid views (e.g. critical realism) attempt to honour both the truth-aspirations and the symbolic depth of religious speech.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
